To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mGluRs in the striatum are involved in the regulation of neuropeptide gene expression; and (2) the mGluR-induced neuropeptide gene regulation is mediated by G-protein coupled second messenger systems.

(1) mGluR activation in the dorsal striatal induces the expression of neuropeptide mRNA in this brain region; (2) the effect of mGluR on the neuropeptide expression is mediated by G-protein and the effect is dose dependent; (3) the effect of the mGluR stimulation is time dependent and biphasic.

1) ACPD increases striatal PPD and SP mRNA expression; 2) PPE mRNA expression is increased in the striatum after ACPD injection; and 3) ACPD induction of striatal PPD, SP and PPE mRNAs is mediated by mGluRs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mGluRs in the regulation of neuropeptide expression in the rat striatonigral and striatopalli-dal pathways.
the regulation of striatal neuropeptides by mGluR.
the effects of mGluRs activation on striatal neuropeptides expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mGluR stimulation by ACPD can increase the expression of PPD/SP and PPE mRNA in rat striatum in a dose and time-dependent manner.
mGluR activation can modulate neuropeptide mRNA transcription in the rat striatonigral and striatopalliadal pathways.
the striatal mGluR is a novel and potentially important modulator of the constitutive expression of PPD/SP and PPE mRNAs in the striatum.

ACPD increases striatal neuropeptides mRNA expression via activation of mGluR.
